chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said, 'In the book of Sama'ah, he raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):'
If something from the urine of a cat touches the garment, then the prayer is not valid in it until you wash it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cat urine on clothes for prayer?
ai.summary: Reported by al-Kulayni from Samaanah, this hadith establishes the invalidity of prayer (salat) if cat urine remains on the garment, emphasizing the necessity of thorough washing for ritual purity. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling highlights the distinct status of cat urine as a minor impurity (najis) that requires removal to validate the prayer, reflecting the practical application of taharah principles derived from the Imams.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira who said, ‘In a book of Sama’at, 
(It has been narrated) raising it to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>:
‘If something from cat urine hits the clothes, so the Salaat would not be correct until you wash it (first)’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah who has said that it is in the book of Sama‘ah who in a marfu‘ manner has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If clothes come in contact with the urine of cats, performing Salah (prayer) with such clothes is not valid until they are washed.’”
